solves.reasoning: From 1번 passage: ③ 'using' is wrong. 'emotions could be ③using to enhance performance' — after auxiliary 'could be', passive voice requires past participle 'used', not present participle 'using'. Correct: 'could be used to enhance'. ①'a means' (noun phrase, correctly used as complement — correct), ②'their' (refers back to students/participants — correct), ④'being used' (passive progressive gerund after 'is' — correct).

From 2번 passage: ② 'visualize' is wrong. 'useful in ②visualize mathematical functions' — after preposition 'in', a gerund (verb+ing) is required. 'visualize' is a bare infinitive/base form and cannot follow a preposition. Correct: 'useful in visualizing'. ①'reflected' (past participle in passive construction — correct), ③'recorded' (past participle in passive 'should be recorded' — correct), ④'whatever' (relative determiner — correct).

From 3번 passage: ③ 'belong' is wrong. 'they prove instead that it ③belong to a class' — the subject 'it' (an important object) is singular third person, so the verb must be third person singular 'belongs', not base form 'belong'. Correct: 'it belongs to a class'. ①'them' (object pronoun referring to 'specific objects' — correct), ②'studying' (gerund after preposition 'of' in 'instead of studying' — correct), ④'similarly' (adverb modifying verb 'reason' — correct).

From 4번 passage: ② 'him' is wrong. 'a patient's trust in the actual drug ②him might be taking' — 'him' is an object pronoun, but here it functions as the subject of the relative clause ('the actual drug [that] him might be taking'). Subject position requires the subject pronoun 'he'. Correct: 'the actual drug he might be taking'. ①'to trigger' (infinitive of purpose — correct), ③'taking' (present participle in 'will be taking' progressive — correct), ④'damage' (bare infinitive after modal 'could' — correct).

From 3번 passage: ③ 'which' is wrong. 'even the objects ③which haven't been defined yet' — after 'even the objects', the restrictive relative clause requires 'that' (not 'which') in this context. The original fullPassage uses 'that' here. 'Even' before the noun signals an emphatic/inclusive relative that favors 'that'. ①'her' (referring to 'An instructor' — the passage uses 'her' for the instructor consistently — correct), ②'which' (in 'conditions under which students exercise' = correct prepositional relative clause), ④'informs' (third person singular, subject = 'he' [Kaptchuk] — correct).

From 4번 passage: ④ 'deterioration' is wrong. '59 percent reported ④deterioration' — the trial result demonstrates open placebos WORK. Reporting 'deterioration' (악화/worsening) directly contradicts the passage's entire point that open placebos outperformed the control group (35%). Correct: 'improvements'. ①'prevent' (monitoring conditions to prevent injury — correct), ②'number' (a number of ways — correct), ③'optimum' (device read to optimum capability — correct).

From 1번 passage: ① 'weaker' is wrong. 'might lead to more effortful punches and ①weaker kicks' — the entire context is about using negative emotions (anger/frustration) to enhance performance. 'More effortful punches' already shows the expected increase; 'stronger kicks' (not weaker) is the logical and contextually consistent parallel. 'Weaker' contradicts the emotion→enhanced effort relationship described throughout the passage. ②'capability' (optimum capability — correct), ③'decimal' (digit to the right of the decimal point — correct), ④'endeavor' (try hard to obtain digits — correct).

From 3번 passage: ③ 'obstacle' is wrong. 'Mathematical calculation ability serves as a key ③obstacle of academic development' — an 'obstacle' is something that blocks/hinders progress (방해물). But the sentence is saying calculation ability serves as a key INDICATOR (지표) of academic level, since it reflects numerical proficiency and cognitive growth. 'Obstacle' is contextually opposite to the evaluative/measurement role described. Correct: 'indicator'. ①'saves' (clustering saves time and effort — correct), ②'particular' (every object has a particular property — correct), ④'seeds' (an apple must have seeds — logically correct from the syllogism).

From 4번 passage: ④ 'remarkable' is wrong. 'The results may seem ④remarkable, but they make the point...' — the passage uses 'modest' to qualify the trial results as not dramatic/spectacular. 'Remarkable' (주목할만한/인상적인) is the opposite of modest (겸손한/보잘것없는). The 'but' clause then pivots to argue the results still matter despite being modest. Correct: 'modest'. ①'trust' (deception triggers trust — correct), ②'up front' (telling patients openly — correct), ③'damage' (discovering deception damages trust — correct).

Choice 2 (doing nothing is more ethical) is not implied. Choice 3 (deception required) directly contradicts the open placebo finding. Choice 1 (individual study) is the opposite. Choice 3 (curriculum stressing abstraction) is not the antecedent. Choice 4 (everyday fruit reasoning) comes after, not before.
